claims.statement: At parent order n=2p+3, the first-mark expansion reduces the marked difference to residuals J_i of order at most 2k+1 (k=p-1); order 2k+1 occurs only for the first mark of degree one, and order 2k occurs only in the two stated three-vertex deletion configurations. For residuals of order at most 2k-1, i_k(J_i)-i_(k-1)(J_i) is nonpositive. An exact sign formula is established for the subclass consisting of k disjoint edges and one isolated vertex.
claims.scope: Structural first-mark reduction at n=2p+3 and exact matching-plus-isolate residual calculation; not the complete favorable-leaf sum.
claims.reason: The result isolates the new odd and even boundary residuals and supplies exact arithmetic for one odd-order forest subclass. No sign theorem for all boundary residuals, guarded tree lift of the matching subclass, or global compensation bound is proved, so the primary assertion remains unresolved.

limitations: No universal sign bound is established for order-2k+1 or order-2k first-mark residuals at this parent order.
No full-sum counterexample or proof is established; local residual signs alone would not decide S(T,p).
The matching-plus-isolate calculation is not shown realizable under the ordinary-tree selector and rank guards.
